messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the console rollout a subset of Editor users can't see the 'Deploy' button or access Project Settings. Looks like a permission-gating regression tied to KMS-enabled projects.

josh: which projects? any common pattern (org, region, key type)?

maria: noticed on two EU projects using customer-managed KMS keys (rotated last week). Not reproducible on hosted-key projects.

carla: hmm, could be a missing permission in the Viewer/Editor role mapping we pushed yesterday. I remember changing the `project.read_keys` bit to be gated by KMS ownership.

ui-eng: saw a console error in Sentry: `PermissionError: missing permiso n project.deploy` (weird spacing because we obf logged). Stack shows check in frontend `/components/ProjectActions` calling `canDeploy(project)` which queries `/api/v1/projects/:id/permissions`.

maria: audit log for one of the affected requests shows: `user: alice, action: list_keys, result: denied` but the audit entry lacks `kms_key_id`. That feels wrong — denied should still log key id metadata.

dan: can you paste the raw audit line?

maria: ```
{"ts":"2026-06-12T15:04:12Z","user":"alice","action":"GET /api/v1/projects/123/keys","result":"denied","reason":"missing_permission","project_id":"123"}
```

dan: confirmed: `kms_key_id` missing. Our audit middleware only appends `kms_key_id` when permission check passes — bug. We should always emit key metadata (sanitized) for forensics.

sec-bot: Opening IR ticket: IR-452 (high) — "audit metadata omission for denied KMS key access". Assigned: dan, severity: P2 -> P1 if evidence of exfil or escalation.

carla: okay for quick mitigation I can: 1) update audit middleware to attach `kms_key_id` on both allow/deny paths, 2) revert the `project.read_keys` gating change in the role matrix to restore Editor Deploy UI until we validate. Which should we do first?

josh: revert role-matrix change first (fast rollback), then fix audit middleware and add tests. Revert will restore UX quickly and reduce incident blast radius.

ui-eng: FYI, I have a tiny frontend PR that assumes backend `permissions` endpoint returns `can_deploy: true/false` — if permission endpoint returns 403 the frontend hides the button. If we revert, we need to ensure endpoint returns 200 with `can_deploy:false` for non-privs not 403.

maria: good call. Dan, can you change backend to return 200 + permission payload even when KMS gating fails (and include `denied_reason` field)? That will let frontend show a disabled button with tooltip instead of disappearing.

dan: yes. I'll push a patch to the permissions service: add `kms_key_id` to audit always, return 200 for /permissions but include `allowed:false, denied_reason:\"kms_key_missing\"`. Adding unit tests and integration test against console.

deploy-bot: deploy started: permissions-service v3.14.7 -> v3.14.8 (canary 3/10 nodes) :rocket:

carla: after deploy we should run the regression checklist: 1) QA repro on two affected projects, 2) confirm audit entries include `kms_key_id`, 3) smoke test Deploy button visibility. I can coordinate QA.

maria: thanks. Also add a short postmortem note in #postmortems once IR-452 closes — include timeline and the role-matrix diff.

sec-bot: IR-452 created at 2026-06-12T15:10:02Z, linked issues: PERF-209, RBAC-87.

josh: long-term follow-ups: (a) add policy-level integration tests for KMS-enabled projects, (b) add audit schema validation in CI, (c) review role-matrix change PR process to require security + UI signoff.

maria: thumbs up. I'll own the post-incident actions. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
